# **Hackathon Plan: Ukrainian Art Meme Platform – Під Склом**

## **1\. Project overview**

We will build a Ukrainian-language website and Telegram bot that turn a user's phrase into a meme made from a public-domain Ukrainian painting, with a short, surprising story behind the artist and the artwork. The goal is to bring people closer to Ukrainian art through humour, with no sign-up required.

**Two core flows:**

1. **Phrase → Painting.** The user types a phrase or describes a situation. The AI picks the best-matching artwork, places the phrase as a caption, and shows 1–2 unexpected facts about the artist and the painting.  
2. **Painting → Caption.** The user chooses a painting from the gallery. The AI suggests 3 funny captions; the user picks one or writes their own.

**Supporting features:** a simple caption editor (position, font, size, colour, outline), download and share, a personal page with saved memes (login needed only to save), an Artists section with extended biographies and artworks, and a Telegram bot with both core flows.

**Key constraints:** 4 people, 7 days, free hosting, Python backend, no model training (we use existing AI APIs with our credits), public-domain artworks only, Ukrainian interface.

## **2\. Team roles (not fixed)**

Each person owns one area end to end, so nobody waits on anyone else for long. Content (the artwork database) is the largest single job, so two people share it in the first days.

| Person | Role | Owns | Helps with |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Person A | Backend \+ AI | FastAPI service, AI prompts, matching (embeddings), caption generation, API docs | Database schema |
| Person B | Frontend | Website pages, meme editor, gallery, Artists pages, login UI, personal page | UI design |
| Person C | Content \+ Data | Artist list, artwork collection, facts, biographies, data import scripts | Fact-checking, pitch |
| Person D | Telegram bot \+ DevOps \+ QA | Deployment, CI, environment secrets, Telegram bot, testing, demo | Content (Days 1–3) |

**Working rules:** one GitHub repo, short-lived feature branches, merge to main at least once a day. Every merge to main deploys automatically, so the live site is always the latest working version.

## **3\. Tech stack and architecture**

Everything runs on free tiers: Vercel for the website, Render for the Python backend and bot, and Supabase for the database, login and image storage. The only cost is AI API calls, covered by our credits.

| Layer | Choice | Why |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Frontend | React \+ Vite \+ Tailwind CSS | Fast to build, huge ecosystem, free hosting |
| Meme editor | react-konva (Konva.js) | Drag text, resize, change colour; exports PNG in the browser |
| Frontend hosting | Vercel (free) | Auto-deploys every push to main, preview link per branch |
| Backend | Python 3.11 \+ FastAPI \+ Uvicorn | Simple, async, auto-generated API docs at /docs |
| Backend hosting | Render free web service | Deploys from GitHub; one service runs both the API and the bot |
| Database | Supabase Postgres \+ pgvector | Free 500 MB, vector search for matching built in |
| Login | Supabase Auth (Google \+ email magic link) | No passwords to store; frontend SDK ready |
| Image storage | Supabase Storage, public bucket | Free 1 GB; \~200 images at \~300 KB each \= \~60 MB |
| Telegram bot | aiogram 3, webhook mode inside FastAPI | No separate server; shares code with the website |
| Server-side image rendering | Pillow | Draws captions for the bot (it has no browser editor) |
| AI | Our provider's API (LLM with vision \+ embeddings) | No training needed (see Section 4\) |
| Fonts | Google Fonts with Cyrillic: Oswald, Rubik, Montserrat, Lobster, Comfortaa | Classic meme fonts often lack Cyrillic; same TTF files used in browser and Pillow |

![architecture · website, bot, backend, Supabase, AI provider][image1]

architecture · website, bot, backend, Supabase, AI provider

The website talks to the backend for AI and saving, and to Supabase directly only for login and images; the bot goes through the same backend, so both share one code path.

**Repository layout (one repo):**

* /frontend — React app  
* /backend — FastAPI app (api/, ai/, bot/, render/)  
* /data — artwork CSV/JSON, import and embedding scripts  
* /docs — this plan, API contract, pitch deck

**Practical notes:**

* Render's free service sleeps after \~15 minutes idle and takes \~30–60 s to wake. Open the site a few minutes before the demo, or ping it with a free monitor (UptimeRobot).  
* Images must load with crossOrigin="anonymous" so the editor can export a PNG.  
* Keep API keys only in Render and Vercel environment variables, never in the repo.  
* Add a per-IP rate limit (e.g. slowapi, 20 AI requests per hour) so anonymous users cannot burn our credits.

## **4\. AI approach (no training)**

We train nothing: a vision-capable LLM describes each painting once, ahead of time, and at runtime the LLM only chooses and writes. Facts come from our own reviewed database, never invented live, so the AI cannot make up false history.

**Step 0 — Prepare once (Days 2–3, script by Person A, review by Person C):** For every artwork, send the image to the LLM and save a short «meme profile» in Ukrainian: what is shown, mood and emotions, 5–10 tags, and 3 everyday situations it could fit (e.g. «коли дедлайн завтра»). A person checks each profile for 10–20 seconds and fixes obvious mistakes.

**Flow A — Phrase → Painting (POST /api/match):**

1. Check the phrase: 1–200 characters, basic moderation (no hate speech or slurs).  
2. Send the LLM the phrase plus a compact catalogue (id \+ title \+ tags for every artwork, \~25 tokens each). For 200 artworks this is \~5,000 tokens, which is fine with our credits and needs no extra infrastructure.  
3. The LLM returns JSON: artwork\_id, a one-line reason it fits, the id of the most fitting fact, and suggested caption position (top or bottom).  
4. The backend loads the artwork, its image and the chosen facts from the database and returns them.

**Upgrade if needed:** if the catalogue grows past \~300 artworks or responses are slow, store an embedding of each meme profile in pgvector, take the top 10 closest matches first, and send only those to the LLM.

**Flow B — Painting → Caption (POST /api/captions):** Send the LLM the meme profile (and the image, if our provider supports vision) and ask for 3 short, different captions in Ukrainian, each under 12 words, as JSON. Ask for variety: one about everyday life, one about work or study, one playful with the painting's own story.

**Prompt rules (system prompt for every call):**

* Answer only in Ukrainian, only valid JSON in the agreed format.  
* Humour is kind: no insults to groups, no war-trauma jokes, no politics about real living people.  
* Never invent facts; choose only from the facts provided.

**Fallbacks so the demo never breaks:**

* If the AI call fails or times out (8 s), Flow A uses simple tag matching in Python and Flow B shows 2 pre-written captions stored for each artwork.  
* Cache results for repeated phrases and the demo phrases.

**Cost check:** about 6,000 tokens per Flow A request and 1,500 per Flow B request. Person A logs token usage per call so we can see how far our credits go.

## **5\. Artwork database**

Target: 15 artists and 150 artworks by Day 5, with a minimum of 60 artworks by the end of Day 3 so development can use real data. In Ukraine, works become public domain 70 years after the author's death, so in 2026 only artists who died in 1955 or earlier qualify.

**Starting list of public-domain artists (verify each before adding):**

| Artist | Years | Why they work for memes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Taras Shevchenko | 1814–1861 | Famous as a poet; few know his paintings and self-portraits |
| Arkhyp Kuindzhi | 1841–1910 | Dramatic moonlight and sunsets |
| Mykola Yaroshenko | 1846–1898 | Expressive portraits and everyday scenes |
| Kyriak Kostandi | 1852–1921 | Scenes of ordinary life |
| Serhiy Vasylkivsky | 1854–1917 | Cossacks, steppe, village life |
| Mykola Samokysh | 1860–1944 | Horses and battle scenes full of action |
| Mykola Pymonenko | 1862–1912 | Village scenes with very expressive faces |
| Ivan Trush | 1869–1941 | Landscapes and sunflowers |
| Oleksa Novakivsky | 1872–1935 | Bright, emotional colour |
| Vasyl Krychevsky | 1873–1952 | Painter, architect, designer of Ukrainian symbols |
| Fotiy Krasytsky | 1873–1944 | Shevchenko's relative; warm genre scenes |
| Oleksandr Murashko | 1875–1919 | Bright portraits; «Карусель», «У червоному капелюсі» |
| Kazimir Malevich | 1879–1935 | Born in Kyiv; the Black Square is perfect meme material |
| Mykhailo Boychuk | 1882–1937 | Founder of Boychukism; tragic, little-known story |
| Oleksandra Ekster | 1882–1949 | Avant-garde, colourful, theatre costumes |
| Heorhiy Narbut | 1886–1920 | Graphic artist; designed the first Ukrainian banknotes and stamps |

Artists to avoid for now because they are still under copyright: Maria Prymachenko, Kateryna Bilokur, Olena Kulchytska, Tetiana Yablonska.

**Where to find images and facts:**

* Wikimedia Commons — use only files marked public domain; save the file page link.  
* National Art Museum of Ukraine (NAMU) and regional museum websites — for titles, years and facts.  
* Ukrainian Wikipedia and publications such as Ukrainer — for biographies; always cross-check facts with a second source.

**Content rules:**

* Each artist: short bio (2–3 sentences), long bio (300–500 words), at least 3 surprising facts.  
* Each artwork: title, year, museum, 1–2 surprising facts, 2 fallback captions.  
* Every fact is 1–2 sentences, has a source link, and is marked «verified» only after a second person checks it.  
* «Surprising» means something a typical person does not know: an unusual model for a painting, a strange event in the artist's life, a hidden detail in the picture.

**Database tables (Supabase Postgres):**

| Table | Main columns |
| :---- | :---- |
| artists | id, slug, name\_uk, birth\_year, death\_year, birth\_place, short\_bio, long\_bio, portrait\_url, sources |
| artworks | id, slug, artist\_id, title\_uk, year, museum, image\_url, thumb\_url, license, source\_url, meme\_profile, tags, fallback\_captions, embedding (optional) |
| facts | id, artist\_id or artwork\_id, text\_uk, source\_url, verified |
| memes | id, user\_id (empty for anonymous), artwork\_id, caption, style (position, font, size, colour, outline), image\_url, created\_at |

**Content pipeline:**

1. Person C and Person D fill a shared Google Sheet (tabs: Artists, Artworks, Facts) — the single source of truth.  
2. A script in /data downloads each image, resizes it to 1200 px on the long side plus a 400 px thumbnail, and uploads both to Supabase Storage.  
3. The AI profiling script (Section 4, Step 0\) fills meme\_profile and tags.  
4. An import script loads the sheet into Supabase. It can be re-run any time; it updates instead of duplicating.

| ID | Story | Done when | Priority | Owner |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| US-01 | As a visitor, I type a phrase and get a meme from a fitting painting | Result appears in under 10 s; caption is placed on the image; a «Інша картина» button shows the next-best match | Must | A, B |
| US-02 | As a visitor, I choose a painting and get funny captions for it | 3 AI captions shown; I can pick one or type my own | Must | A, B |
| US-03 | As a visitor, I see the story behind my meme | Under the meme: 1 fact about the painting, 1 about the artist, link to the artist page | Must | A, B, C |
| US-04 | As a visitor, I adjust the caption | Drag to move; change font (5 options), size, colour, outline; top/bottom presets; up to 2 text blocks | Must | B |

| US-06 | As a visitor, I use everything except saving without an account | No login prompt until I press «Зберегти» | Must | B |
| US-07 | As a user, I log in quickly | Google or email magic link via Supabase; logout works | Must | B, A |
| US-08 | As a user, I save memes and see them on my personal page | «Мої меми» shows a grid of my memes, newest first; I can open, download and delete them | Must | B, A |
| US-09 | As a visitor, I browse all artists | Artists page: portrait, name, years, short bio for each | Must | B, C |
| US-10 | As a visitor, I read about one artist | Artist page: long bio, facts, all their artworks; each artwork has a «Зробити мем» button | Must | B, C |
| US-11 | As a visitor, I use the site on my phone | All pages usable at 375 px width; editor works with touch | Must | B |
| US-12 | As a Telegram user, I send a phrase and get a meme \+ story with image | Bot replies with the finished image and the story in under 15 s | Must | D, A |
| US-13 | As a visitor, offensive input is politely refused | Hateful or abusive phrases get a friendly message, not a meme | Must | A |
| US-14 | As a visitor, I browse and search the gallery | Filter by artist, search by title or tag | Should | B |
| US-15 | As a Telegram user, I pick a random painting and choose a caption | /random shows a painting with 3 caption buttons; tapping one returns the meme | Should | D |
| US-16 | As a visitor, I share a meme by link | Saved memes get a public link with a preview image | Should | B, A |

**Internal story (team):** as a content editor, I update the Google Sheet and re-run the import script, and the site shows the new content without code changes. Must, owner C.

## **7\. Schedule (7 days)**

The website and bot are live on the internet by the end of Day 1 and every day after that, so deployment is never a last-day surprise. Replace «Day 1–7» with real dates once the hackathon dates are known.

![7-day schedule · 4 people, 5 phases, 4 checkpoints][image2]

7-day schedule · 4 people, 5 phases, 4 checkpoints

Each checkpoint (diamond) is a team check at the evening check-in: if it is not met, the next morning's standup decides what to cut. The detailed tasks with IDs are in Section 8\.

**What «done» looks like at each checkpoint:**

* **Live skeleton (end of Day 1):** the site opens on a Vercel link and shows data from the Render backend; the bot answers in Telegram; Supabase tables exist.  
* **Core flows live (end of Day 3):** Phrase → Painting and Painting → Caption both work on the live site with 60 real artworks; the bot sends a finished meme.  
* **Feature freeze (end of Day 5):** all «Must» stories work live; after this, only bug fixes and content.  
* **Demo (Day 7):** two full rehearsals done, backup video recorded, project submitted.

## **9\. Risks, definition of done, demo checklist**

The biggest risks are slow content collection and AI answers that are unfunny or wrong; both have a fallback planned from Day 1\.

| Risk | What we do | Owner |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Content takes longer than planned | Two people on content Days 1–3; 60 artworks is enough for a demo; 150 is a stretch goal | C |
| AI invents false facts | Facts only from our verified table; the AI only picks which fact to show | A |
| Captions are not funny | Test 30 phrases on Day 5; tune prompts; keep 2 hand-written captions per artwork | A, C |
| AI API is slow or down during demo | 8 s timeout, tag-matching fallback, cached demo phrases | A |
| Render free service is asleep at demo time | Uptime monitor; open the site 5 minutes before; backup video | D |
| Copyright question from judges | Public-domain artists only; licence and source stored for every image | C |
| Cyrillic text renders as boxes | Use only fonts with Cyrillic; test «ґ є і ї» in browser and bot on Day 2 | B, D |
| Anonymous users use up our credits | Per-IP rate limit; cap on phrase length | A |
| Last-minute merge breaks the site | Feature freeze end of Day 5; Days 6–7 only bug fixes | All |

**A task is done when:**

* It is merged to main and works on the live site (or live bot), not only on a laptop.  
* Someone other than the author has clicked through it once.  
* Texts visible to users are in Ukrainian with no placeholders.

**Demo checklist (Day 7):**

* ☐ Website and bot are awake and on the latest version  
* ☐ 3 rehearsed demo phrases that give great results (cached)  
* ☐ Show Flow A, the editor, the story card, saving to «Мої меми», an artist page, and the bot  
* ☐ Backup video ready in case the internet fails  
* ☐ Links ready: site, bot, GitHub repo, pitch deck  
* ☐ One-sentence pitch: «Українське мистецтво через гумор: напиши фразу — отримай мем і історію за ним»
